bullets.title: Fed near-certain to hike Sept 16; 2-3 more expected through 2027 as DM central banks broadly tighten
bullets.body: August core CPI printed +0.29% m/m (consensus 0.20%), core PCE tracking ~22-24bp — sufficient to push September FOMC hike probability to 85-92% across desks. JPMorgan, Wolfe, and Piper all shifted base cases to Sept AND Dec hikes; JPM economists add Sept to prior Dec forecast. ECB already hiked 25bp to 2.50% with Oct/Dec hike highly likely; BoJ expected to hike to 1.25% next week. JPM's global economists note 8 of 9 DM central banks projected to hike by year-end, with Taylor rule suggesting DM rates ~100bp too low. 10-year Treasury yields briefly touched 4.97%, near Oct 2023 cycle highs; 2-year above 4.63%.

bullets.title: Oil surges to ~$100/bbl on Iran escalation; diesel at all-time highs, stagflation risk elevated
bullets.body: Brent briefly topped $108 this week on Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and US-Iran naval clashes — Saudi production collapsed to 6.2 MMBo/d (lowest since 1990). US diesel prices hit $6/gallon for the first time. Wolfe and 22V flag oil as the 'dominant factor' driving 10-year rate and P/E re-ratings globally. Piper and JPM note Houthi control of Bab el-Mandeb coast and a 3-4 mb/d supply deficit; Iran crude stock outside blockade fell from 90M to 29M barrels. Goldman raised Brent/WTI year-end targets by $5 to $85/$80 but flagged $120 tail risk. Geopolitical backdrop remains primary macro force through year-end.

bullets.title: Inflation re-accelerating broadly: core PCE ~30bp above Fed comfort zone, tech goods now additive
bullets.body: 22V and Hedgeye both flag consensus core PCE now ~30bp — well above the Fed's 15bp comfort threshold — with underlying inflation running 100bp+ above target. August PPI and CPI both surprised upside; supercore services +0.51% m/m (highest since Jan). Critically, AI-driven tech goods have swung from a -0.1pp to +0.1pp contribution to global CPI; DRAM ASPs +259% YoY and NAND +344% are passing through to PC, consumer, and enterprise hardware costs. JPMorgan estimates $1 oil increase adds 3-4bp to inflation — the oil move from $87 to $94 alone could add 21-28bp to Q4 CPI.

bullets.title: US equities down ~0.8% on week but resilient vs. rate moves; positioning reset creates potential upside
bullets.body: S&P 500 fell -0.8% w/w (+11.9% YTD) while small caps (Russell 2000) dropped -2.4%; equal-weight meaningfully underperformed. Despite the 2-year yield surging 26bp (largest weekly move in over a year), SPX outperformed rate-implied moves by 2.1% on a two-day basis — a 3-sigma event per Morgan Stanley. Hedge fund net leverage retreated to 52% (25th percentile), providing a downside cushion; corporate buybacks running at +65% w/o/w with 85% via 10b5-1 plans. Goldman's prime services note TMT stocks saw the largest 2-week long buying since June 2025 (97th percentile 5-year).

bullets.title: AI capex supercycle intact: MSFT tripling to 38GW by 2032, ORCL OCI +121%, NVDA guiding +70% FY27
bullets.body: Microsoft plans to triple data center capacity from ~12GW to 38GW by 2032, adding ~4-4.5GW annually. Oracle F1Q27 cloud infrastructure revenue surged +121% YoY to $7.4B, booking $30B+ in new AI contracts and building RPO to $664B (+46% YoY). NVIDIA CEO reaffirmed 70% revenue growth for FY27 and estimates global AI infrastructure spend reaching $4T by 2030. TSMC August revenue +53.3% YoY. OpenAI paused new Pro tier subscriptions due to 'unprecedented' Astra model demand. UBS Taiwan tech data shows hyperscaler capex revised up to +95%/+43% YoY for 2026/27E.

bullets.title: Rates-equity correlation turning positive; bond market losing diversification role for 60/40 portfolios
bullets.body: 22V and JPMorgan both flag that rising bond yields are now positively correlated with equity weakness — the traditional portfolio hedge is failing. JPMorgan's ERP has compressed to 2.1%, the lowest since 2002, meaning equities are more sensitive to yield moves and rebalancing from stocks to bonds becomes attractive. Systematic macro strategies (Vol Target, CTA, Risk Parity) are at full allocation (81st percentile leverage) and could sell $12bn on a 1% SPX rally. Bloomberg Commodity Spot Index at all-time highs; 22V notes 'commodity bull markets are built on fear.'

bullets.title: Market rotating from non-AI cyclicals into AI buildout and momentum; consumer discretionary hit hardest
bullets.body: Multiple desks (22V, Goldman, UBS) confirm rotation: AI-exposed momentum/earnings factors up 2%+ long-short over two weeks while Consumer Discretionary, homebuilders, airlines, and restaurants are net sold to multi-year low L/S ratios. XLY is below both 50- and 200-day MAs; 59% of consumer discretionary stocks have Weak/Poor technical scores. Rate-sensitive sectors including housing stocks (ITB at Technical Score 0, all names below 50-day MA) continue to underperform. 22V recommends XLY put spreads as a hedge given TSLA's 18% weight and Oct 22 earnings risk.

bullets.title: Consumer sentiment plunges; gas prices key near-term headwind while high-income consumers hold up
bullets.body: UMich September consumer sentiment collapsed to 47.8 (vs. 52.5 consensus), the second-lowest level on record, with year-ahead inflation expectations jumping to 4.6%. PSC and JPMorgan consumer trackers show softening across all five confidence internals as gas prices rose. JPM August spending data shows a $20B wallet headwind from elevated gas (forecasted $4.45/gallon avg) Sept-Dec. However, high-income/discretionary spending is still running +5.4% YoY in August with a 2-year stack of +10.3% (strongest YTD). Lower-income cohort (~30% of Academy Sports' base) pulling back.

bullets.title: AI-driven agentic commerce reshaping internet sector; SHOP, BKNG, DASH, EXPE under pressure
bullets.body: Meta's Muse personal AI agent launched and immediately hit #2-3 on the iOS App Store with usage 10x above internal testing cohorts. JPMorgan upgraded META to Overweight ($820 PT) on models and agents. The launch sparked sharp selloffs in OTA stocks (BKNG, EXPE, ABNB down 8-18% from recent highs) and commerce intermediaries (SHOP -7%, DASH -5%). Mizuho and Shopify management argue Muse actually routes through Shop Pay, retaining SHOP's economic interest; Shopify catalog converts 2x better than web-scraped results in LLM shopping. The agentic commerce inflection is driving fundamental debate across the internet sector.

bullets.title: Software/SaaS index (IGV) down ~4% YTD vs S&P +13%; rates and AI disruption fears weigh on multiples
bullets.body: All-SaaS index multiples compressed -4.9% week-over-week to 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales; IGV is down -0.7% YTD vs S&P 500 +13.6%. Higher rates are the primary multiple headwind, with software most rate-sensitive given duration of cash flows. AI disruption fears are amplified by OpenAI's ChatGPT for Financial Services launch (bundling SEC filings and private company data) and the Astra model's PCB design demo (which briefly sold off EDA stocks CDNS/SNPS). Wolfe TMT conference notes only ~5% of enterprise customers are on highest SaaS editions; AI monetization is still early but Agentforce/Claudeforce partnerships signal real traction.

bullets.title: Semiconductor AI infrastructure cycle remains strong; NVDA GPU contract renewals at +20% premium
bullets.body: ORCL disclosed it is renewing multi-year-old GPU contracts at an average 20% premium, validating AI compute pricing power. Compute market pricing has moved from $10-15M/MW to $20-25M/MW for longer-term contracts; spot pricing is $40-50M/MW. TSMC August revenue +53%, tracking at the high end of Q3 guidance. Memory prices surging: DRAM contract prices forecast to rise 13-18% in Q3; Samsung/SK Hynix inventories below 10 days of supply. SOX outperformed last week (+4.16%); hardware/networking names (GLW +15.5%, HPE +14%, CIEN +10%, DELL +12%) surging on data center demand.

bullets.title: ECB hiking cycle underway with Oct/Dec hike likely; European recession risk if oil stays elevated
bullets.body: ECB hiked 25bp to 2.50% as expected; JPMorgan forecasts one final hike in December (October live if data surprises). ECB's 2027 core inflation forecast revised up to 2.6% from 1.9% — above their 2% target through 2028. EU gas storage in Germany/Netherlands is below seasonal norms; the risk is price not shortage given adequate LNG access. 22V notes European recession risk if oil prices grind higher into winter. ECB mispriced at four hikes according to Jefferies; UK likely to hold in September but shift language toward November hike. BOJ expected to hike to 1.25% next week.

bullets.title: VIX range-bound near 15; options market pricing ~1% SPX move on CPI; volatility below significance given macro calendar
bullets.body: VIX settled around 15-16 entering the week, well below levels that reflect the macro event density (FOMC, BoE, BoJ next week; midterms in Nov). 22V recommends VIX call spreads as sensible tail hedges. SPX put buying into CPI pushed near-term implied vol from 10 to 20, creating a +58% premium vs 30-day realized vol. JPM options implied a +/-1% SPX move on the CPI print. Hedgeye technical: SPX immediate-term resistance at 7,670; Russell 2000 broke to bearish trade and trend.

bullets.title: BoE expected to hold next week but signal November hike; UK GDP surged 0.4% in July on AI/tech
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects BoE to hold at 3.75% with a 6-3 vote, but to shift language hawkishly toward November given energy pressures and growth resilience. August CPI likely at 3.2% YoY, well above BoE's 2.8% forecast; CPI could peak around 4% or higher by early 2027. UK July GDP rose 0.4% m/m — computer programming and consultancy services surged 3.5% m/m driven by AI adoption. JPM revised 3Q annualized UK GDP up from 0.8% to 2.0%, and 2026 full-year from 1.5% to 1.8%.

bullets.title: Geopolitical risk intensifying: US-Iran military exchanges mark new escalation threshold
bullets.body: Multiple US-Iran military exchanges occurred this week including Iranian ballistic missile attacks on US Navy vessels and US destruction of IRGC crude tankers. Wolfe DC policy analysis sees no quick diplomatic exit: Iran has reconstituted ballistic missile production, US interceptor stockpile is depleting, and Houthis control the Red Sea coast. Goldman warns of $120/barrel oil risk if attacks intensify. The 'muddle forward' equilibrium with intensifying pain on both sides is the base case. This is identified as the dominant macro force for EM through year-end by JPMorgan.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi summit Sept 24 seen as key geopolitical catalyst; trade, tech controls, Taiwan in focus
bullets.body: President Trump and President Xi are set to meet September 24, with trade, technology controls, Taiwan, capital flows, and supply chains likely in focus. US-China AI talks are also scheduled for September. The November 1 trade truce agreement expiration and ongoing US restrictions on Chinese AI firms (Anthropic alleging Alibaba ran 'largest-ever distillation attack') create a charged backdrop. China's copper tariff threat (no longer a 'foregone conclusion' per ROTH) and the EU-China trade deficit near €1bn/day are additional pressure points.

bullets.title: Midterm elections: Nov outcome could reshape AI regulation, data center policy, and fiscal path
bullets.body: Multiple research teams flag the midterms as a key risk/catalyst. Goldman notes S&P 500 historically averages +14.5% return from end-August to end-March in midterm election years. Progressive policy repricing risk (wealth/asset taxes, AI regulation) is the bear case; a split Congress makes legislation harder but shifts attention to executive action. Data center moratorium activity is intensifying as a November election issue (Wells Fargo), and 69% of Americans oppose local AI data centers. Post-election SPX returns historically: +5.4% (3mo), +11.4% (6mo), +14.7% (12mo) since 1990.

bullets.title: Real estate and rate-sensitive sectors underperforming sharply; 30-year mortgage back above 7%
bullets.body: S&P 500 RE Index fell 1.10% on the week vs. -0.80% for S&P 500, with 10-year yields rising 19bp to 4.97% and the 30-year fixed mortgage rate hitting 7.12% — highest in over a year. Existing home sales hit the slowest pace since June 2025; inventory at 1.62M units (highest since late 2019). REIT subsectors: Office REITs -3.39%, Multi-Family -1.27%, Retail -2.12%. Data Centers eked out a small gain. Housing affordability is at the 15th percentile historically; Hedgeye notes the 2-year and 10-year yields are at cycle highs, with the 10-year approaching the key 4.98% (Oct 2023) resistance level.

bullets.title: Power/utilities sector outperforming as AI data center demand drives structural electricity consumption surge
bullets.body: EIA forecasts record US power consumption of 4,270 TWh in 2026 and 4,349 TWh in 2027, driven by data center development. S&P 500 Utilities +1.7% on the week vs. S&P -0.8%. Bloom Energy added to S&P 500 effective Sept 21 (+9.6%). ERCOT Batch Zero process advancing with Core Scientific receiving ~1GW of base load classification and IREN's Sweetwater Hub conditionally included with 1.4GW energized. Nuclear getting attention: NEE's Duane Arnold nuclear restart secured a $1.9B DOE loan; South Korea reportedly nearing a $100B+ deal for up to 8 US nuclear plants.
